'''''Nemophila menziesii''''', known commonly as '''baby blue eyes''' or '''baby's-blue-eyes''',<ref name="BSBI07">{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17}}</ref> is an annual herb, native to western [[North America]].<ref name="Sullivan2018">{{cite web | url= http://www.wildflowersearch.com/search?&PlantName=Nemophila+menziesii | last= Sullivan | first= Steven. K. | date= 2018 | title= ''Nemophila menziesii'' | website= Wildflower Search | accessdate= 2018-07-06 }}</ref><ref name="Jepson">{{cite web | url= http://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/cgi-bin/get_IJM.pl?tid=Nemophila%20menziesii | date= 2018 | title= Nemophila menziesii | website= in Jepson Flora Project (eds.) Jepson eFlora | publisher= Jepson Herbarium; University of California, Berkeley | accessdate= 2018-07-06}}</ref>

Historically, it was eaten by cows kept by the [[Kawaiisu]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Menzies' Baby Blue Eyes |url=http://naeb.brit.org/uses/23631/ |access-date=2025-06-17 |website=Native American Ethnobotany Database}}</ref>

==Distribution==
The plant is native to [[California]], [[Baja California]], and [[Oregon]].<ref name="Sullivan2018"/>

It grows virtually throughout California at elevations from sea level up to almost {{convert|6500|ft|m}}. It grows in many types of [[habitat]]s, including [[chaparral]], valley [[grassland]]s, and montane locales.<ref name="Jepson"/><ref name="Sullivan2018"/>

==Description==
''Nemophila menziesii'' is variable in appearance. Lower leaves are stalked, lobed and oppositely arranged, {{Convert|10|-|50|mm|1}} with five to thirteen lobes, each entire or with one to three teeth. Upper leaves are more or less sessile and less lobed than lower. The stalk of the inflorescence is {{Convert|20|-|60|mm|1}}. Calyx lobes are {{Convert|4|-|8|mm|1}}. The flower is blue with a white center or all white, usually with blue veins and black dots near the center. It is {{Convert|6|-|40|mm|1}} wide. The tube is less than or equal to the filaments.

===Varieties===
The species includes three [[variety (biology)|varieties]]:<ref name="Jepson"/>
*''Nemophila menziesii'' var. ''atomaria'' has white flowers with black dots, often with a faint blue tint or blue veins in the corolla. It is found on coastal bluffs or grassy slopes in Oregon, Northwestern California, the Central Coast of California, and the [[San Francisco Bay Area]].
*''Nemophila menziesii'' var. ''integrifolia'' has blue flowers, with black dots at the center and deep blue veins. It is found in grasslands, canyons, woodlands, and slopes in the Central Coast, southern Coast Ranges, southwestern California, east of the [[Sierra Nevada (U.S.)|Sierra Nevada]] range, and into the [[Mojave Desert]] and Baja California
*''Nemophila menziesii'' var. ''menziesii'' has bright blue flowers with white centers that are generally dotted with black. It is found virtually throughout California, in meadows, grasslands, [[chaparral]], woodlands, slopes, and desert washes, but it does not occur above {{convert|5200|ft|m|abbr=off|sp=us}}.

==Cultivation==
It is also cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]], as annual wildflower in [[native plant]], [[xeriscape|water conserving]], traditional, and [[wildlife garden]]s.

It can occasionally be found outside its native range as an [[introduced species]], such as in [[Alaska]].<ref name=usda>[https://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=NEME USDA PLANTS]</ref>
